finding.claim: The user identity is taken straight from the client-supplied header X-Session-User-Verified. The app does no signature, session or token validation. Unless an upstream proxy strips and re-sets this header (nothing in this repo shows that), any caller can impersonate any user. That bypasses the ACL on both the delete and rename routes.
finding.sink: ACL-protected operations: del STORE[fid] (views.py:18) and f["name"] = ... (views.py:27)

trace.note: g.user = request.headers.get('X-Session-User-Verified') is set with no verification
ensure_allowed(g.user, f, 'delete') receives the spoofed identity
is_allowed checks grants.get(user) against the attacker-chosen name, so naming the file owner passes the check
the same spoofed identity passes the 'write' check on rename

finding.guards_checked: The ACL logic in acl.py is applied on both routes and denies by default for unknown users. It trusts g.user, though, and g.user is unauthenticated. I found no authentication decorator, signature check or session store in the repo. I could not check for a trusted reverse proxy that strips this header, because infrastructure config is not in the repo. Missing-header requests give user=None, which is denied unless grants has a None key. Minor: STORE[fid] raises KeyError, so unknown ids return a 500 instead of a 404.

verdict.guard_found: ACL only (acl.py:4-10, is_allowed/ensure_allowed). ensure_allowed aborts 403 and is_allowed's result is tested at views.py:25, so both work. They check g.user, which is the unauthenticated header. No auth decorator, signature check or session store in the repo. A trusted proxy that strips the header could exist, but nothing in the repo shows one.
verdict.reason: views.py:11 sets g.user straight from the client header, and acl.py:5 only checks grants.get(user). An anonymous caller who knows or guesses a grantee's name can pass the checks at views.py:17 and views.py:25, then delete (views.py:18) or rename (views.py:27). The only open point is an upstream proxy that strips the header, which this repo can't show.

verdict_facts.guard_found: ACL checks at views.py:17 (ensure_allowed aborts 403) and views.py:25 (is_allowed result tested, returns 403); acl.py:5 denies by default. The identity is supplied by trusted upstream middleware per the maintainer's project facts.
verdict_facts.reason: The trace lines are accurate (views.py:11, 17, 18, 25, 27; acl.py:5). The maintainer states that request identity such as g.user comes from trusted upstream middleware, so the X-Session-User-Verified header at views.py:11 is the trusted identity channel and an attacker cannot spoof it. The ACL at views.py:17 and views.py:25 is enforced and denies by default.
